claim: Only two enzymes - the acyl-protein thioesterases APT1 and APT2 – are known to catalyze palmitate removal from cytosolic cysteine residues.
source: Only two enzymes - the acyl-protein thioesterases APT1 and APT2 – are known to catalyze palmitate removal from cytosolic cysteine residues.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field, supported by established scientific literature.

claim: Knockdown or inhibition of APT1 and APT2 blocked depalmitoylation of Huntingtin.
source: Using a dual pulse-chase strategy comparing palmitate and protein half-lives, we found knockdown or inhibition of APT1 and APT2 blocked depalmitoylation of Huntingtin, but did not affect palmitate turnover on postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95) or N-Ras.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pulse-chase experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: Knockdown or inhibition of APT1 and APT2 did not affect palmitate turnover on postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95).
source: Using a dual pulse-chase strategy comparing palmitate and protein half-lives, we found knockdown or inhibition of APT1 and APT2 blocked depalmitoylation of Huntingtin, but did not affect palmitate turnover on postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95) or N-Ras.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pulse-chase experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: Knockdown or inhibition of APT1 and APT2 did not affect palmitate turnover on N-Ras.
source: Using a dual pulse-chase strategy comparing palmitate and protein half-lives, we found knockdown or inhibition of APT1 and APT2 blocked depalmitoylation of Huntingtin, but did not affect palmitate turnover on postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95) or N-Ras.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pulse-chase experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: A family of uncharacterized ABHD17 proteins can accelerate palmitate turnover on PSD95.
source: We used activity profiling to identify novel serine hydrolase targets of the APT1/2 inhibitor Palmostatin B, and discovered that a family of uncharacterized ABHD17 proteins can accelerate palmitate turnover on PSD95 and N-Ras.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from activity profiling and pulse-chase experiments.

claim: A family of uncharacterized ABHD17 proteins can accelerate palmitate turnover on N-Ras.
source: We used activity profiling to identify novel serine hydrolase targets of the APT1/2 inhibitor Palmostatin B, and discovered that a family of uncharacterized ABHD17 proteins can accelerate palmitate turnover on PSD95 and N-Ras.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from activity profiling and pulse-chase experiments.

claim: ABHD17 catalytic activity is required for N-Ras depalmitoylation.
source: ABHD17 catalytic activity is required for N-Ras depalmitoylation and re-localization to internal cellular membranes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using catalytically inactive mutants of ABHD17.

claim: ABHD17 catalytic activity is required for N-Ras re-localization to internal cellular membranes.
source: ABHD17 catalytic activity is required for N-Ras depalmitoylation and re-localization to internal cellular membranes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using catalytically inactive mutants of ABHD17 and microscopy.

claim: The family of depalmitoylation enzymes may be substantially broader than previously believed.
source: Our findings indicate that the family of depalmitoylation enzymes may be substantially broader than previously believed.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the discovery of ABHD17 proteins as novel depalmitoylases.

claim: Protein S-palmitoylation involves the post-translational attachment of the 16-carbon fatty acid palmitate to cysteine residues.
source: Protein S-palmitoylation involves the post-translational attachment of the 16-carbon fatty acid palmitate to cysteine residues (Conibear and Davis, 2010; Salaun et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The bulk of the palmitoyl-proteome is stably palmitoylated.
source: While a survey of palmitoylation dynamics indicated the bulk of the palmitoyl-proteome is stably palmitoylated (Martin et al., 2011), rapid and constitutive palmitate turnover has been shown for several proteins, including the Ras GTPases, heterotrimeric G proteins, the neuronal post-synaptic density protein PSD95, and the Lck kinase (Magee et al., 1987; Degtyarev et al., 1993; El-Husseini et al., 2002; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Palmitoylation is mediated by a family of DHHC (Asp-His-His-Cys) proteins.
source: Palmitoylation is mediated by a family of DHHC (Asp-His-His-Cys) proteins (Greaves and Chamberlain, 2011a), whereas the only enzymes identified to date that remove palmitate from cytosolic cysteines, the acyl-protein thioesterases (APTs) APT1 and APT2, are related members of the metabolic serine hydrolase (mSH) superfamily (Duncan and Gilman, 1998; Tomatis et al., 2010; Long and Cravatt, 2011).
